data.gender_notes: Sulpicia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'sulpicare', meaning 'to weigh or judge'. In Christian tradition, Sulpicia represents a person with clear insight and precise judgment. The name Sulpicia carries the meaning “Precise, bright, or clear sight” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sulpicia usually hope their child will grow to embody precise, bright, or clear sight and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: סולפיציה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: סולפיציה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו ברומי, והוא נגזר מהמילה 'סולפיקס' שפירושה 'רגל' או 'עקב'. השם סולפיציה משויך לרומאית העתיקה ומעיד על קשר עמוק עם האדמה והיצירה. לנוצרים, השם מייצג יצירה, התחדשות וגדילה רוחנית.

in_greek.name: Σουλπικία
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Σουλπικία σημαίνει πνευματική εμβάθυνση
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Σουλπικία είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την αρχαία Ρώμη και σχετίζεται με τη λέξη 'sulpix' που σημαίνει 'πόδι' ή 'τακούνι'. Το όνομα αυτό αντανακλά τη σύνδεση με τη γη και τη δημιουργία. Για τους χριστιανούς, η Σουλπικία αντιπροσωπεύει τη δημιουργία, την ανανέωση και την πνευματική ανάπτυξη.

in_latin.name: Sulpicia
in_latin.long_meaning: Sulpicia is a Christian name derived from ancient Roman 'Sulpicius', related to 'sulpix' meaning 'foot' or 'ankle'. The name Sulpicia reflects a connection to the earth and creation. For Christians, Sulpicia represents creation, renewal, and spiritual growth, signifying a deepening spirituality.

data.cultural_impact: Sulpicia is primarily known in Christian history for St. Sulpice, a Benedictine abbot and patron saint in the late 5th century. He is the founder of the Sulpicians, an order of priests dedicated to pastoral ministry and education. This name has historical and cultural significance for the Roman Catholic Church, representing the dedication to the spiritual wellbeing and intellectual growth of its followers.
data.spiritual_significance: With the name Sulpicia, one can ponder the spiritual importance of living a life full of discernment and introspection. In this sense, the name symbolizes the ongoing process of spiritual growth and development. Sulpicia is believed to be a reminder that every action has consequences that need to be weighed carefully, providing a deep sense of responsibility and commitment to serve others faithfully.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sulpicia is a Latin name meaning "of the full moon." In Christian tradition, it is believed to represent the wisdom and nurturing qualities associated with the maternal figure of the Virgin Mary, who is likened to the full moon in her capacity to illuminate and provide sustenance.

historical_references.reference: Sulpicia, a celebrated Latin poetess, is known to have lived in the late 1st century AD. She is believed to have been a member of the noble family of the Cornelii Lentuli, and her poetry is characterized by its erotic and sensual themes.

Another Sulpicia is mentioned in the 'Historia Augusta', a late 4th-century work. This Sulpicia is said to have been a beautiful Vestal Virgin who was seduced by the emperor Elagabalus around AD 221. She was banished to Capua and eventually killed herself.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Sulpicia' is most commonly associated with a poet from ancient Rome whose works have been the subject of modern interest in several areas. Her poetry, which is believed to be devotional in nature, has been studied by scholars on platforms such as Academia.edu and Goodreads for their historical and literary value. Additionally, feminist interpretations of Sulpicia's poetry have gained popularity in modern times, shedding new light on the role of women in ancient Roman society. The Poetry Foundation also features Sulpicia's works, showcasing her contributions to the rich tradition of Roman poetry.
